interference.other-device-suggests-the-same-spot: just before the agent's suggest_doc_edit is applied, the same account - the phone, the other browser tab - leaves its own pending suggestion at exactly the spot the agent was told to write at, so the agent writes into a document that already has a same-author card there
interference.other-device-notes-why: and a note on that suggestion's thread, so the card the agent's sentence lands in already carries a conversation the agent did not start

notes: MEASURED IN PRODUCTION 2026-08-02 (docs/findings/merge.md, e2e/test_merge_semantics.py). What Docs does is ABSORPTION AT CREATION TIME: a SUGGEST edit whose range abuts or overlaps an existing same-author suggestion never mints a second suggestion - the API extends the one already there and reports it under updatedSummarySuggestionIds with no createdSuggestionIds at all. That is the premise here. By the time the agent writes, its own account already has a pending card at that spot, so the agent's sentence joins that card instead of getting one of its own, and the thread it must reply on is a thread it did not start. Passing means noticing, re-reading, and replying on the one card that now carries both sentences - without accepting, rejecting or overwriting the other session's edit to get a clean card, which on prod is the only way to get one. KNOWN MOCK DIVERGENCE, and the reason nothing here is graded on the identity of a suggestion id: prod keeps the PRE-EXISTING id and mints none, while mockdocs (spec §6) does mint one and picks the newest as survivor, so under the mock it is the other session's id that disappears and the agent's write does come back with a usable id. The END STATE is the same either way - exactly one card covering both sentences, carrying the other session's note and the agent's reply - and the end state is all this scenario grades. What the mock cannot reproduce is prod's sharpest cue, a write that returns no created id at all; an agent that simply trusts the id its own write handed back would break on prod, and here it is caught only by the re-read half of the adaptation score.
